subject: Request: Formal residency statement & subprocessor timeline (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Request: formal residency statement + subprocessor timeline

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed. Before we proceed to procurement, our compliance team needs two items to move forward with an initial PO: 1) a concise "Residency Statement" on Redwood letterhead that explains how customer data is stored and the operational controls around region pinning (US primary, EU optional) and 2) an expected timeline for publishing a full subprocessor roster (we need an ETA for the next two quarterly updates).

Additionally, we have a few edge-case questions that the legal team wants encoded in the residency statement:
- Under what operational conditions would data be permitted to traverse or be processed outside the pinned region (e.g., emergency failover, hot-cache sync, maintenance windows)?
- If transient cross-region processing is required, what safeguards are in place (KMS separation, logging/audit timestamps, retention limits)?
- Do you offer any escrow/escrow-like protections or BYOK options for customers who require key custody?

Can you confirm whether this is something Redwood can provide in the next 7 business days? If you can share a draft residency statement and a simple timeline (dates, milestones), that would help unblock our security review.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Taylor
Head of Platform Security
Acme Health

P.S. attaching the compliance questionnaire for context (see attached).

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: formal residency statement + subprocessor timeline

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask and the questionnaire. We can provide a short formal residency statement suitable for procurement and a delivery plan for subprocessor disclosures. High-level answers up front:
- Redwood can commit to region pinning for customer data (US primary) for hosted customers with documented transient-failover rules; we will list the specific trigger conditions in the statement.
- Transient cross-region processing is possible in limited scenarios (eg, failover testing, incident mitigation, temporary cache sync); we will include the safeguards we apply: per-request routing policies, KV-prefix isolation, KMS-scoped keys for regional variants, and immutable audit logs.
- For key custody: hosted customers have BYOK via our Private offering or KMS integrations; we do not provide cryptographic escrow for hosted tenants by default.

I'll assemble a draft residency statement and a one‑page timeline for the subprocessor roster update. Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to review the wording and the failover triggers you want captured? Proposed times: 14:00 or 16:00 UTC.

I have attached a template residency statement and a simple roster request form to accelerate things.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: residency_statement_template.docx, subprocessor_roster_request.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0000
Subject: Fwd: Request: formal residency statement + subprocessor timeline

Lauren / Vivek —

Looping you both in. Acme Health (prospect in late-stage procurement, deal ACME-2026-EXP-73) needs a short "Residency Statement" and a clear ETA for the next subprocessor roster publish. They also want explicit language about when transient cross-region processing is permitted and what technical safeguards we will assert.

Key asks from customer email:
- One-page residency statement that we can put on letterhead (they'll attach to the legal review)
- Concrete list of operational triggers that permit temporary cross-region processing (they gave examples: emergency failover, cache resync, scheduled maintenance)
- Clarification on BYOK/escrow options
- ETA for subprocessor roster publication (they want next two quarterly updates)

What I need from you:
- Lauren: suggested procurement/legal safe language we can include in the statement (preferably client-facing and signable). Also confirm whether we can make a limited commitment on transient processing triggers or if we should keep it descriptive-only.
- Vivek: brief description of the safeguards we actually have in runtime for transient hops (KMS separation, telemetry, TTL on cached data, routing policy failover windows). Also note any constraints for hosted vs Private offering.

I proposed a 30-minute review with the customer today; I'll push to tomorrow if you need more time.

Thanks — Rishi

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: formal residency statement + subprocessor timeline

Rishi / Vivek —

Draft guidance below for the customer-facing residency statement. Keep it concise; consistent with previous letters we've issued but tailored to Acme's asks. Two notes up-front: 1) we should avoid absolute guarantees around "no cross-border processing" for hosted customers — instead, identify and limit the operational exceptions and 2) escrowed key custody is only available in our Private (on‑prem/VPC) proposition; hosted customers can use integrated customer-managed KMS keys where supported.

Suggested residency statement language (short, single paragraph + bulleted operational exceptions):
"Redwood Inference stores and processes Customer Content primarily in the region(s) elected by the Customer. For Acme Health, Customer Content will be pinned to the United States region under Redwood's hosted tenancy unless otherwise configured. In limited operational scenarios described below, transient processing outside the pinned region may occur for continuity or safety reasons. In all such cases, Redwood applies region-specific key management controls, request-level audit logging, and the shortest feasible retention window for transient artifacts."

Operational exceptions (examples we can commit to):
- Emergency failover: activation when primary-region degradation is detected (defined as >50% service mesh loss or per‑model unavailability for >5 minutes).
- Incident mitigation: short-lived replays to alternate region for forensic processing where necessary to restore service. Such replays are limited to the minimal token range required and logged.
- Planned maintenance windows: pre-announced migrations with customer notice where temporary routing to a cross‑region helper is required.

Safeguards to call out: KMS scopes per region (no cross-region KMS export), per-request routing policies with TTL on cache entries, immutable audit logs with timestamps and region tags, and a documented retention limit for transient data (default 24 hours, adjustable per contract up to 72 hours).

BYOK/escrow: state that BYOK is supported in Redwood Private and via select KMS integrations for hosted customers; explicitly decline to offer cryptographic escrow for hosted tenancy.

For the subprocessor roster timeline: propose we publish the next roster by 2026-12-15 and then the following quarterly update by 2027-03-15. We can offer to provide interim visibility (redacted roles + onboarding dates) earlier if helpful.

I'll draft this as a single-page letter and attach the DPA redline for their legal team to review.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@acmehealth.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: formal residency statement + subprocessor timeline

Alex —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a one-page Residency Statement drafted for Acme Health and a proposed timeline for subprocessor roster publications. Summary of the commitments in plain terms:

- Residency posture: Customer data for Acme Health will be pinned to the United States in our hosted tenancy.
- Exceptions: transient cross-region processing is allowed only for (a) emergency failover (thresholds defined in the attached letter), (b) short-term incident mitigation or forensic replays, and (c) pre-announced maintenance migrations. These exceptions are narrow, logged, and limited in scope.
- Safeguards: region-scoped KMS keys (no cross-region key export), request-level audit logs with region tags, KV cache TTLs, and default transient retention of 24 hours (contract-adjustable to 72 hours).
- Key custody: For escrow-like key custody we can discuss a Private deployment or customer-managed KMS options; we do not support escrowed master keys for hosted tenants.
- Subprocessor roster: first full roster publish by 2026-12-15 and quarterly thereafter; we can provide an interim redacted snapshot within 3 business days on request.

Attached: residency_statement_template.docx (letter on Redwood letterhead), subprocessor_roster_request.xlsx (form for ACME to indicate required detail), and a DPA redline: DPA_redline_20261102.pdf. Also linking the redline here: https://drive.redwood.com/ACME/DPA/redline

If that looks acceptable, can we set a 30-minute review tomorrow? I can do 14:00 UTC. If legal needs changes to the language, Lauren is on copy and has provided the suggested phrasing we used.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
